title: CiviCRM keeps membership, donation and event data as mutable rows behind an optional, thin logging module
content:
CiviCRM-class membership tooling stores memberships, donations and event registrations as rows that are updated in place. The research adds the detail that decides the case: the logging module is optional and thin, so even where it is switched on the trail is a side-channel rather than the system's spine.

The consequence is that the membership lifecycle — joined, lapsed, reinstated, upgraded, refunded — can be read as a current state but not reconstructed as a history. For an organisation whose obligations follow from that history, a row is the wrong shape of evidence: it says what is true now and is silent about when it became true and who made it so.

SYSTOPIA's business is a delivery practice built on this tooling, which places the gap at a layer they already control. The move is not a replacement CRM but an auditable record sitting under the lifecycle events the CRM already produces, which keeps the proposal additive to the practice they sell.
